independent_qa.note: Internal adversarial re-derivation and second-implementation checks; not external peer review.

claim_boundary.note: The #635 example refutes only a canonical-neighbour proof template. It does not refute the known asymptotic result. No accepted closure proof was found defective.

results.strongest_result: Exact Mahler identities prove v2(C_12(z))=5, v2(C_20(z))=7, and v2(C_28(z))=10 for every integer z; equivalently v2(A_24(x))=17, v2(A_40(x))=27, and v2(A_56(x))=38 for every integer x.
results.remaining_gap: These are the first fixed certificates with nontrivial odd cores 3,5,7 in the missing third layer, but the all-s Cartier doubling law and any uniform control over variable block length remain unproved. Squares N in the original variable-k problem remain open.
results.verification: higher_cartier_mahler_certificates.py; exact Fraction construction of the full degree-m polynomials and Mahler coefficients; independent direct SymPy series check for all three listed m

results.strongest_result: For every nontrivial modulus split, the quotient occupies at least two residue fibres, so E(A)>=4m_q and norm(P)>=sqrt(8m_q); hence a Tang equality tuple has m_q<=n/2 for every q unless q divides all exponents. At the critical m_q=n/2 split it has exactly two active fibres and both are ideal Prouhet-Tarry-Escott equality chains. If the r outside residues are additionally dissociated, the exact formula E(A)=2^r E(C) holds and forces a ternary residue relation in every equality split except n=2.
results.remaining_gap: The majority-divisibility theorem gives a strict constant improvement on a broad subclass but does not force any m_q>n/2 in an arbitrary primitive tuple. Nor is there a global theorem forcing a high-rank dissociated residue split; the universal sqrt(n) order is unchanged.
results.verification: residue_copy_decomposition.py; 8007 exponent multisets, 38235 nontrivial modulus splits, and 3679 dissociated directions, zero failures; non-dissociated sharpness and two Tang-equality controls

results.strongest_result: For interior vertices, canonical Hall matching is equivalent to the odd-endpoint graph being a pseudoforest. A solver-free independent 10-point set in only valuation layers 1 and 4, with every upper neighbour in range, has 10 canonical edges on 8 vertices and Hall deficiency 2; three proper-divisor neighbours yield an explicit full matching. Every standard two-layer commuting square also has a proper-divisor exit.
results.remaining_gap: One must choose proper-divisor exits globally across overlapping multi-cycle components and handle nonstandard cycles and boundary vertices. Canonical directions, two layers, and boundary repair alone are insufficient.
results.verification: canonical_bicycle_counterexample.py; all 45 independence pairs, endpoints, connected cycle rank, full matching, and 1393 standard-square regressions checked with solver-free integer arithmetic

results.strongest_result: For actual forbidden wrap differences W in any finite abelian decoder group, 2^g*kappa(W)<=|G|, where kappa is the largest K with nonzero K-K contained in W. Universal intervals recover the previous log k loss, but a middle-third set W of size Theta(p) has kappa=2 and admits an explicit binary decoder of rank log2(p)-O(1) avoiding W.
results.remaining_gap: The actual zero-fibre recursion has not been shown to produce wrap sets with bounded clique number, nor has cumulative clique loss been made O(1). Thus the pointwise floor(log2 n) conjecture remains open.
results.verification: reachable_wrap_packing.py; 3130 dissociated cyclic decoders through modulus 21 plus exact p=11,17,101 middle-third clique and explicit-decoder controls
